nodes.name: Ni film codeposition
nodes.procedure: A Ti foil (50 um thickness) was cleaned by sonication in acetone and isopropyl alcohol for 10 min and rinsed in distilled water for 10 min. Prior to the deposition, the vacuum chamber was evacuated to a pressure of 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ Torr. The Ni film catalyst was fabricated on the Ti foil using electron beam evaporator with deposition rate of Ni (0.5 Å s⁻¹) until the total thickness reached 75 nm with the substrate rotation speed of 25 rpm.

nodes.name: Fe-Ni film codeposition
nodes.procedure: A Ti foil (50 um thickness) was cleaned by sonication in acetone and isopropyl alcohol for 10 min and rinsed in distilled water for 10 min. Prior to the deposition, the vacuum chamber was evacuated to a pressure of 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ Torr. The Ni-based bimetallic thin film catalysts (Fe-Ni) were deposited on the Ti foil using an electron-beam evaporator combined with a thermal evaporation source. The electron-beam evaporation of Ni and thermal evaporation of Fe dopants were carried out simultaneously with precise controlled deposition rates of Ni (0.5 Å s⁻¹) and Fe (0.03 Å s⁻¹), which were monitored by quartz crystal microbalance (QCM). The deposition proceeded until the total thickness reached 75 nm with the substrate rotation speed of 25 rpm. The composition of the oxophilic metals in Ni matrix was controlled to be about 5%.

nodes.name: Cr-Ni NHs oblique angle deposition
nodes.procedure: A Ti foil (50 um thickness) was cleaned by sonication in acetone and isopropyl alcohol for 10 min and rinsed in distilled water for 10 min. The Cr-Ni NHs array was directly grown on the Ti foil by OAD method using a custom-designed electron-beam evaporator equipped with a thermal evaporation source for a co-evaporation process. Prior to the deposition, the vacuum chamber was evacuated to a pressure of 1 × 10⁻⁶ Torr. The electron-beam evaporation of Ni and thermal evaporation of Cr dopant were carried out simultaneously with precisely controlled deposition rates, which were monitored by QCM: Ni (1.9 Å s⁻¹) and Cr (0.1 Å s⁻¹). During the codeposition, the vapor flux incidence angle with respect to the surface normal axis of the substrate, the oblique angle, was maintained at 80°, and the substrate was rotated for 2s at 1 rpm and stopped for 12s, repeatedly to form an array of NHs.

nodes.name: Ni NHs oblique angle deposition
nodes.procedure: A Ti foil (50 um thickness) was cleaned by sonication in acetone and isopropyl alcohol for 10 min and rinsed in distilled water for 10 min. The Ni NHs catalyst was fabricated through the same OAD process on Ti foil without thermal evaporation of Cr. Prior to the deposition, the vacuum chamber was evacuated to a pressure of 1 × 10⁻⁶ Torr. The electron-beam evaporation of Ni was carried out with precisely controlled deposition rate of Ni (1.9 Å s⁻¹), monitored by QCM. During the deposition, the vapor flux incidence angle was maintained at 80°, and the substrate was rotated for 2s at 1 rpm and stopped for 12s, repeatedly to form an array of NHs.
nodes.source_text: The Ni NHs catalyst was also fabricated through the same process without thermal evaporation of Cr.

nodes.characterization_summary: Synchrotron XRD shows fcc Ni (111) and (200) peaks at 44.5° and 51.8° for Ni NHs; Cr-Ni NHs shows broadened Ni peaks with reduced intensities, no detectable Cr phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4c shows XRD patterns measured by using a synchrotron X-ray source... For Cr-Ni NHs, no detectable trace of Cr is observed, but the Ni peaks are broadened with reduced intensities

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms nanohelical geometry of Cr-Ni NHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image shown in Figure 4d further confirms the nanohelical geometry of the Cr-Ni NH

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows lattice fringes with d-spacings of 0.20 nm and 0.18 nm corresponding to (111) and (200) planes of cubic Ni phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image shown in Figure 4e indicates the lattice fringes with d-spacings of 0.20 and 0.18 nm, corresponding to the (111) and (200) planes of the cubic Ni phase

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms ~5% Cr atomic ratio in Ni NHs matrix with homogeneous elemental distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mappings (Figure 4f) show the homogeneous distribution of Cr elements within the Ni NH matrix. ... energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis further confirms the existence of Cr element with the atomic ratio of about 5% in Ni NHs

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks: Ni⁰ at 852.4 eV (2p₃/₂) and 869.7 eV (2p₁/₂); oxidized Ni at 853.5 eV and 855.9 eV; Cr 2p shows Cr³⁺ at 577.2 eV and 575.9 eV; Cr/Ni atomic ratio 1.58:27.06 (~5%). Cr incorporation increases oxidized Ni ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 5a, the high-resolution Ni 2p spectra consists of Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ core-level emissions, in which the peaks located at 852.4 and 869.7 eV are identified as metallic Ni⁰. By deconvolution of the Ni 2p₃/₂ core-level spectra, the peaks at 853.5 and 855.9 eV... are attributed to the oxidized Ni species... Figure 5b shows the Cr 2p core-level spectrum measured from the Cr-Ni NHs with two peaks at around 577.2 and 575.9 eV corresponding to Cr³⁺ states

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni L₃,₂-edge XANES shows increased peak intensities for Cr-Ni NHs vs Ni NHs, indicating more unoccupied Ni 3d states and increased Ni valence due to Cr doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiL₃,₂-edge XANES profiles are assigned to the transitions from the Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ ground states to the unoccupied Ni 3d final states... the increased peak intensities of the Cr-Ni NHs relative to that of the Ni NHs are attributed to larger amounts of the unoccupied Ni 3d states

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM reveals increased surface roughness and surface area of Cr-Ni NHs compared to Cr-Ni film.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Topographic measurement using atomic force microscopy (AFM) reveals increased surface roughness and hence an increased surface area of the Cr-Ni NHs compared to the Cr-Ni film
